utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the witness, Mr. Usher?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have problems hearing. I have noise in my headphones, problems with hearing, interruptions. The sound is interrupted. Now it's okay. I did have noise in the ear phones and the sound was interrupted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric. Your direct examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I have too many microphones around me, probably due to technical problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I shall be calling you Witness during my examination. The Trial Chamber has granted some protective measures for you. The first is a pseudonym, and the second is face distortion. That is why I'm going to ask the usher to give you a piece of paper with your first and last name on it. Don't read it aloud, just say "yes" if it is indeed your name. Try to make a pause before you start giving your answer. Sometimes I will even show you with my hand whether you can start giving your answer. This will help our interpreters, because we speak the same language and they will be able to interpret more accurately. Just say "yes" or "no" now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, for the sake of the record, the pseudonym of this witness is MT, am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance, Mr. President. Can we now move into private session, during which the witness is going to give us information about himself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, during the Serbian aggressor's attack on Mostar, were you militarily engaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In which HVO unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: In the 4th HVO Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Until when were you in that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Until spring, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: After that, where were you engaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I was in the main logistics of the city HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where were you when the conflict between the HVO and the BH Army broke out in Mostar? That was in May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters missed the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When did you return to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Two or three days after the beginning of this conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you join a unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I came as a volunteer and joined Vinko because they were my friends and my neighbours, and I offered my services to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, we lost something in the transcript. When you asked, "Where were you when the conflict between the HVO and the BH army broke out in Mostar, that was in May, 1993," we lose the answer from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I can see it in the transcript. I do not manage to follow the transcript, so I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where were you when the conflict broke out that was on the 9th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I was in my native place, Grude [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: The transcript shows it wrongly so it is not the native place but the place of work. If you can slow down, the interpreters will find it easier to follow. So was it your native place or the place where you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll do something about the transcript, and I just hope you make a pause between the answer and the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must say that now I have some interruptions in my ear phones, Mr. President, so the sound is not very good. Something is wrong with this point. My colleague Par had some problems yesterday as well. This thing on the desk is not functioning. I've moved it but now I have interruptions in my headphones. Can I please try to use these headphones to see how we go with them? We shall see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that you joined Vinko. Can you explain when you say, "Vinko," who is it and when was it more precisely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: My wife was from Grude. I lived in Mostar. I would go to work to Grude. Sometimes I would sleep in Mostar, sometimes in Grude, and two or three days later, I arrived in Mostar, there were my friends and neighbours there, Vinko himself was there. They gathered to defend that part of the city. I arrived some five or six days later, joined the unit, and stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: We -- I don't know who it was officially but Vinko was the centre point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did he later on become the commander formally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What was the name of your unit at the beginning, at the beginning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Mrmak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What was your task, your duty, in the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I was in charge of the logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you please assist the Chamber and tell us how strong was the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: There were about 35 to 40 men in the unit. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What was the task of your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: The task was to man the line on the Bulevar. And to defend it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photo, 14.5. Can you please show us and mark the segment of the line, i.e., the part of the Bulevar that you manned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who was with you on the line, which units? Who was on the left, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It was the 3rd --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Left on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: The Benko Penavic unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And on the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: The home guards, the military police, the 3rd Ilic Brigade and they worked in shifts. Every ten days, they would change place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the part that you marked, did all these buildings exist in 1993, especially I have in mind the time of the conflict between the BH Army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, but one was in the meantime extended, the pink one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did they look the same as they do in this photo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: These here did look the same but that one over there was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Have they been reconstructed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us how did your unit man the line? Were there shifts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes. There were shifts, 8 to 12 hours a day was one shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How many soldiers were there in one shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: 10 to 15. Sometimes all of them if there was something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you know at the time, and do you know now, who was in charge of these shifts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: There were some formal group leaders who changed their places, who swapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you give us a name or a nickname of any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Dubi, Dolma, Brada, Campo, Nedjo, and that is all I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know their full first and last names? We will move into private session if you wish.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I can try.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Can we move into private session just for precaution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the unit was formally established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It was in mid-May or the second half of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was your unit in charge of the area deep in the background, in the back of this line that you marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you please wait until the counsel finishes the question and then start giving your answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, since when have you known Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Since my childhood, since we were children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was Vinko Martinovic's deputy in the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: He was always there. There was no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Finish your sentence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: He was always there so there was no need for anyone to stand in for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what would soldiers do once they finished their shift and leave the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Like this. For instance a shift would be eight hours, so eight hours they would be here on standby, in this building, and eight hours they would be free. So practically they were free only eight hours, and of course they went home, took a rest, slept.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you have barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: We did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you describe to us your uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I brought my own, of course. Everybody brought whatever he had. Later on, we were given some green trousers, blouses, and T-shirts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How were the soldiers issued their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, it was against a receipt. For instance, every soldier had to sign whatever he had been issued with, and then had to return it. That is how it was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Part of our answer when you said you returned it to a place, tell us where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: That undersigned paper, this paper that had been signed by a soldier, I took it back to Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was there in Grude, especially since you told us that that is where you worked? What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It was the main logistics of the HVO for the whole BH, the armament, equipment, money. Specifically I brought I would take a lorry from Zagreb and then drive around because I worked there. Assistance arrived there, food.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let's go back to the uniforms. Were the soldiers issued camouflage caps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Why, it was summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did the soldiers receive salaries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Not in the beginning. Later on we began to receive some salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And how was it paid out? Can you describe it to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Like this. Since we, that is those other groups are around us, they would be there for seven days and they would have seven days off or ten days and I would go up there because I knew those who worked up there. I asked -- I asked how could we resolve this, and he told me to bring a list of the soldiers at the end of every month, and that is how it would be done. So we would get money on the first and I would take it down there and then it was distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did the soldiers have to sign that they had received the money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: As a rule, yes. Sometimes somebody would take on somebody's behalf and then he would sign it. Somebody didn't want to because they had to take the paper back. I couldn't, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you describe to us your routine workday of a logistics man in the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I slept at home, naturally I came in the morning, I saw what kind of food was needed, and then I took it from the rest and then I would go to the restaurant where we all had -- ate and then I would supply it with whatever was needed, and I see what else the troops needed, the gear and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You used an acronym, MTS what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, MTS is a Yugoslav word, which means materiel and it covers everything that concerns a soldier -- all soldiers' needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the photograph which you have before you. When you joined the unit, were there any obstacles, any barriers around the health centre and on Liska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you point at them and mark them, too, and tell us what they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: All that I saw?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All that you saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: There were some sandbags, that is where we enter. That is the path that we took. Then there were what do you call them, hedgehogs, isn't it? Somewhere here. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as you can remember.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: And in the early days, when I came there, there was a bunker that we had, and next to it there were some boards and some bags. It was quite a sound barrier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were there any trenches around the health centre and by this I mean next to this red line that you drew.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No. This is all concrete. I don't know how you could -- no, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, some witnesses said they had to dig trenches right there, and under gunfire too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was fighting a daily occurrence on the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, at times more, at times less. Attacks.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the witness please speak into the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you ever on the line personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I didn't go there often. Once, twice, sometimes I didn't go into this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And in your daily contact with soldiers in your unit, did you see them being afraid? And what were they afraid of most? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: They were afraid of the snipers the most, from these buildings here, because some jihad music was aired there and the mujahedin were threatening and throwing some Bosnian pots that blow up, and they even sent once a car with a remote, which exploded, or sent explosives through the sewage. There was something every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any prisoners were brought to the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where were they brought?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know who brought them there, how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: To our unit. Dinko Kenezovic was responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Which means of transportation was used to bring them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: They had a truck and a van.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many would be brought from Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, depended on the order, 10, 20, 30, how many they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know what they did and who assigned them to jobs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: They worked with cars, cleaned, tidied up, armoured our cars for the front line, made coffee, made barbecue and things on the front line down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: As a logistics man, did you have anything to do with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Nothing special. For instance, if I brought food from Grude, then I'd -- they would help me to unload it or unload it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did they sleep at the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, a couple of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how was it organised, this sleeping?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: They slept on the floor above us. It is a normal, three-room flat with a kitchen and there were beds, those who wanted to stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you remember something about how -- what was the food like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: From the town defence, they got their rations but they ate in the restaurant because those guys who were not on the front line of course sometimes they could go there, sometimes they couldn't, so they made a barbecue down there, but there would always be food left over and they would take that. I know for instance a friend from Stolac, whom I knew from before, he was always there and he was there, and he ate the same thing as we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you slow down? Because they cannot follow you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, that's how I always...

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What did you tell us about this friend from Stolac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I said that we had food in a restaurant which existed before the war and which is still now, and where the woman prepares home-made food, so he was with us and he ate and he even put on weight.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was any of them -- did any of them get killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I am not sure -- nobody -- some were wounded but somebody was killed, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember any wounding cases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes there was a man who was wounded behind me as I was entering the base, he and two soldiers, by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Oh, come on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: His nickname, his name, his last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I simply can't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you describe to us what happened after that wounding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, he was hit by a shell on the road at the entrance to the base, he was behind us and we took him to the hospital and later on, there were two of our soldiers across the street, and there were also put by some others in the car and we drove them away. He was hit in the thigh.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did he survive? Did he recover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, he did. It was just a shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When we talk about these prisoners from the Heliodrom, do you have any recollection whether they had any visitors or whether they went home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, those here who were there, the local ones, ours, from Mostar, of course, I mean who would come to those who were outsiders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: According to you, did anyone mistreat them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I don't know, no. I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did they get any remuneration for the work that you told us they did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Specifically, we gave them cigarettes, which we didn't smoke because we got them, it was -- I don't know what it was called, Partner [phoen], and every one of us whose car he repaired give him some -- give him some clothes or something. We didn't have much. We were not particularly well off either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But what you could see, how did Vinko Martinovic treat them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Quite normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were they taken to work by the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: They were taken down there as I have said to make coffee and barbecue and clean up the standby base and things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Could you show us where that went on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: This building, which burnt later on, but we were here in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were they exposed to any kind of gunfire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No. It was 150, 200 metres away, and they were also bags so that...

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You know, the indictment alleges that they had to perform heavy manual labour on the front line and under gunfire. What would be your comment to that? Are you aware of anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of the name and last name, Nenad Harmandic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What do you know about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: May I say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It says here that I didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: No, it's quite all right. Look at line 19. It says, "Yes, I have." It means yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, it was a little late.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What do you know about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Like this: Exactly when he was with us, brought from Heliodrom, I had returned from my trip to Germany with a truck, and I called those prisoners who slept there to distribute some parcels with food and some clothes and I saw a new man, I didn't know him before, I saw that he was all covered in bruises and I asked who he is and they said such and such, brought from Heliodrom, and I asked who beat him, and I asked who beat him, and they laughed. I offered him something but he wouldn't anything. When I left with my truck and came back and when I returned they asked where is he and they said he's not here they took him back. Where? They took him to the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you hear the first and last name, Halil Ajanic nicknamed Lopata?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about when he came as a prisoner to the base of the unit?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We could not hear the witness's answer because he speaks over the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, we missed the answer from this witness. I believe that both of you have to slow down so that the interpreters could catch up with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you please repeat your answer? I will repeat my question. What do you know about a -- when Halil Ajanic, Lopata, came as a prisoner to the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: He didn't come there as a prisoner. He came later when his son was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What do you know about that occurrence which you mentioned, his son's death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: He was, I don't know how, but he was pals with two of our soldiers, and they were together in that flat, and the kid was toying with weapons and something went off, I don't know what, a bomb or whatever, and he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know what soldiers were involved?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: They were those two Germans, Otto, Rudo, Udo, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to those foreigners, what happened to them, after that event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: When it happened, this one's father came and Stela said, what? Because we didn't know what had happened and naturally he didn't have money because I guess he had been in prison. They let him go and then he gave him to buy and then he called the police, I don't know whether the military or the other one, to see over there and to solve and he said that they couldn't stay with us because they were not careful. But we do not know what exactly what happened. We didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But with all the speed, don't be angry and I have to warn you. You swallow up your words and your syllables and the interpreters cannot interpret all that you say.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could not hear the witness's comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Tell us, what happened when Halil Ajanic came to see Vinko Martinovic? What is it that he gave him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: He gave him 150, 200 marks, 300, doesn't matter, to buy the coffin. And to perform that ritual that they have, that funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what happened to those soldiers, to those foreigners? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: We called the police because nobody knew who was the kid or what had happened, whether it was sabotage or something, and later on, that is how it happened that the boy had touched something but they were not with our unit any more, they were told that they were not needed and that we didn't need such people with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Who said it to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But otherwise, what was their status in the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Those two Germans?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I don't mean Germans only, I mean the foreigners who were with the unit. Did they enjoy any privileges or what was their status there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Normal, like any other soldiers. They went to the front line, they were on standby, they would have time off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how they communicated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Poorly. Well, I drove so I knew a little, but I didn't know. Well, Germans mostly hands -- they were brought to the front line arrow, point at a particular area -- kuke [phoen], that is what we called it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you have in your unit somebody who served as their interpreter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how they communicated with Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No how, poorly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did they go to the front line next to the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Like all the other soldiers, they would go 8 hours, 8 or 10 or 12 hours standby and the same, the front line, and they slept or walked around.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what shifts they were on, who was their commander, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, it changed all the time because the order come those danger then everybody is it at the front line and then they are not and then they change, one didn't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember -- I mean those foreigners in the unit, how long were they, with the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Two or three days, fifteen, a month. These two were a month or two, not longer, if he didn't stay there a month, he didn't get pay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the prisoners. Do you know whether there was an order to bring them there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I will ask Madam Registrar and Mr. Usher to show you P551.1, Prosecution's Exhibit. It is a binder 2, January this year. Page 01537684.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you find the page in the right, upper-hand corner, it says, vertically 01537684. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Very well. Will you tell us what it is about and what date the order bears?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: 9 September, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Yes, 9 September.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: These are orders. These are the orders to go and fetch prisoners. This is the order of the Mostar Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, keep it. Keep this order and I'll ask Madam Registrar and Mr. Usher to show you P601. Page 01535189. So you have the number in the upper right corner, 01535189. Or 88 perhaps is before it, the last two digits. Have you found it? 01535188, or 189.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: But the first last number is 222.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: 601. It's the book containing the names of detainees at the Heliodrom, so this is P601. Not one of those 17 first binders but [In English] January of this year. [Interpretation] Two binders from January last. 601.1. [In English] My mistake, my apologies. 01535188 or 89. Shall I give the witness my copy, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if Madam Registrar could not find it at this moment, you may use your copy. But Mr. Seric, you have to inform Madam Registrar what kind of documents you are going to use during your direct examination before the start of the trial so that she could be well prepared for that document. Otherwise, we just lost a lot of time in finding those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I did so, but these are two books that we are talking about, so maybe my instructions were not really precise, when I was announcing the documents that I was going to need. It is not the right one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which number did you mention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you find the list of soldiers for the Vinko Skrobo ATG dated 9th September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Look at number -- the number of detainees and compare it with the order that you saw a little while ago, bearing the same date, 9th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: There are 37 soldiers here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How many on the order?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I'm not sure if anyone else in the courtroom is in my situation, but I don't know which document that we are now comparing these numbers to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have no idea either, maybe you could go to private session and put that document on the ELMO so everybody could know which document you're using, Mr. Seric. Well, I was informed the document is P567.1, rather than P601.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure that I have made a mistake, Your Honours. We can put the both documents on the ELMO. The previous order with date of 9th of September, and this list of detainees. And we can move into private session to do that. The first document is a sequence of orders under number 551.1, and the order that we saw a little while ago, that the witness has, is page number 01537684. Because several orders share the same number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we will go to the private session and Mr. Usher will put that document on the ELMO, so that we could see which document we are using right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember 17th September, 1993? And any attempts of any action on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have D2/17 or P608, Prosecution number? Can we have the document shown to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Is that information A?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What date does the information refer to? What does it say in the first sentence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: The action of the HVO on the 17 September, 1993. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you please slow down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It is the information of the assistant commander of the OZJIH for SIS.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: On that day, did you personally go to the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I want to note for the record our objection to this testimony. The summary of this witness has never said anything about this witness testifying about the 17th of September. There is simply no information, no notice given to the Prosecution at all, and I think the Chamber will note from the past several weeks this seems to be a recurring problem and the Prosecution made known its views months ago about the inadequacies of these summaries. So we are now in a topic of examination on which the Prosecution has been provided no notice, or prior statement whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, I also read the statement of the summary of this witness. It is indeed that this incident was not mentioned in your summaries. But at this stage, I will let you ask some questions concerning the incidents that happened that day and we will see if the Prosecution is in a position to do the cross-examination later on. If not, I'm afraid we have to give him some time for the preparation of the effective cross-examination on what happened on that day. You may continue, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. However, I cannot not say this: If our summary says that it is a soldier who was in the unit throughout the conflict between the HVO and BH Army, it is impossible to conclude that he did not participate in all the actions. If this is going to be objections on the part of the Prosecution, then I have to raise the issue of objectivity on the part of the Prosecution, and before I continue, Mr. President, my proposal would be that we have a break now and that I continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt and get on my feat but Mr. President, I want to respond to that. That is clearly not the purpose for which these summaries are contemplated under Rule 65 ter. If that was the case all that any party would have to do is simply say in this case was this witness was a member of the Vinko Skrobo unit, period. And we would soon be put on notice of anything that might have happened during 1993 in that unit. That is not the kind of summary that the Rules of this Tribunal calls for. I also point on the same page of the summary of this witness and I won't mention his name but item -- Witness number 22, this is -- in that summary, there is specific evidence -- excuse me, notice given that that witness would testify on the last line, "And the events of 17 September, 1993." So it's clear that with all respect to my learned friends, it's clear that notice -- they are capable of giving notice and the kind of generic notice that we have objected to in the past as insufficient and I must say it's surprising to finds ourselves in approximately the last two weeks of the Defence evidence in this trial which started by the way, I might add, one year ago yesterday, and be having this discussion now. We object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have taken notice of your submissions and the statements on this issue, and we have the summaries at our hands at this moment. But we have already made a decision. We will ask Mr. Seric to continue with the questions on the incidents and later on we will see whether the Prosecution is in a position to do the cross-examination or not. I think it's time for a break, so we'll have our break and we'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: We mentioned the events on the 17th of September, 1993. Do you remember, do you personally know, whether on that day, they were detainees from the Heliodrom in the bases?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter missed the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I think they were in the base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, we did not catch the answer of the witness for your first question. Will you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: My first question was whether there were any detainees in the base.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: An action was planned so they didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, during the break I was warned by the interpreters and asked to tell you that you should slow down and that we should make a break between my question, your answer, and my next question. I am going to give you a sign by hand when I want you to start answering. So please do not rush into your answers. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please be shown Exhibit 612.1? That is the Prosecutor's Exhibit P612.1, which is connected with that particular day and some events on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please read this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Aloud?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Yes, aloud. Slowly so that the interpreters can follow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: "Pursuant to the letter sent to the main staff of the HVO on the 24th of September, 1993, hereby I submit the following information. In keeping with the order number 03/18/93, dated 17 September, 1993, which was issued by the commander of the defence of the town of Mostar, Mr. Zlatan Mioyelic, the Vinko Skrobo ATG has taken over 30 detainees for work. The security for these detainees is provided by Mr. Dinko Kenezovic. ID number AA40802. 20 September, 1993, at 2000 hours, 18 detainees were returned from work. Their security from Varda to the Heliodrom was provided by the military police whose commander was Nikola Vidacko. On the 27th September, 1993, the remaining 12 prisoners were returned. They had been kept at work for ten days."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Who has signed this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Josip Praljak, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask Madam Registrar to show the witness Exhibit P601.1, page 01535272?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, what date does this list of prisoners refer to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: 17 September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In the right-hand column, can you look at the detainees who left, who were taken over by the Vinko Skrobo unit? How many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What does it say at the end of the signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It says, "Taken by Dinko Kenezovic, ID number, AA40802, signed by, returned on the 27th September, at 1940 hours."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Is this signature consistent with the report that you have just read, that you read a little while ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I never paid any attention to this. You should ask him. There were never any objections to any orders, there were no special orders. I've never seen this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: All right. My next question: The Prosecution alleges that some of the detainees on that particular day were wearing camouflage uniforms, that they were armed by wooden rifles, that they were used as human shields and that they crossed over to the other side. What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I heard that only subsequently, when the indictment was issued, and this is really ridiculous, to use human shields against a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Are these allegations in keeping with the report that you have just read?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: What allegations?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What they crossed over, and in that report it says that they were returned to the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, it says so on the list. That means that this is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Okay. We can remove this -- these two exhibits. The next topic of my examination is the following. Did the Vinko Skrobo ATG belong to the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, we did not get your answer. Would you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know who issued orders to Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: The commander of the town defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you personally see any of these orders or did you hear them if they were given verbally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: If they were verbal, they arrived several times when they expected some attacks on any of the sides, from any of the directions, and when some reinforced security measures were ordered, then it would arrive in written form. There would always be somebody arriving from them to issue verbal orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Who was it whom you saw most frequently to come to the base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: The commander of the town defence. I think it was Zlatan, most Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. often. But, in any case, I knew him best.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You didn't give us his full name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Zlatan Mijo Jelic so-called.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us - although you have already mentioned something like that in one of your previous answers - where did you physically get the money for your salaries?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It arrived from the headquarters in Grude which was the headquarters for the entire HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, now we are going to show you Prosecution Exhibit P704. Towards its very end almost, can you please find page number 00795386?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It would help the interpreters if this was put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Have you found it? Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In the upper, left corner, it says, "The Convicts Battalion." How do you account for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe for administrative purposes we were put there. Maybe for the purpose of salaries. We were the Vinko Skrobo ATG. That is what my salary list read. I've never seen anything like this before. This is on the 2nd of December. Dinko Kenezovic, who was killed in November. And here I can see him on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What is the number under which you find Dinko Kenezovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the last page under 81?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes. Again Dinko Kenezovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with all the names in the list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No, not with all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you explain the names that are unknown to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Okay. We won't need this document any longer. Witness, did you hear, during the war or perhaps later, that some people impersonated members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I heard it two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you please finish? What was it two or three times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: That somebody impersonated somebody falsely said he was a member of Vinko Martinovic's and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Vinko Martinovic helped Muslims? If you do know about that, do you know of any example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I do. He let at the request of the town commander, a young man who was under age, who was at the Heliodrom, and we were guarding him, and he let him go, and our neighbours, like I do, we lived there together. They lived the whole life. What can they do?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did you personally help anyone? I mean Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Same way. None of us was financially so powerful too. How can you help him but what food we had, we shared cigarettes. Our neighbours, we don't know what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know or do you remember whether there were cases of disobedience in the unit? I mean soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And if something happened like that incident with Halil Ajanic's son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Then you had leave the unit because whether somebody was late for the shift, it would be taken out of his salary and it would be distributed amongst others, those who were in his group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, until when were you with the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, until Washington or what's it called? February, March, 1994, when the cease-fire was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there were any military checkpoints in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Not in the town itself. There was only the police and so, but they were outside the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which checkpoints were there outside the town and where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Shall I give you these localities or the directions where the road stretched?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You can do both.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: There was towards Medjugorje, Miljkovici, towards Siroki Brijeg at Zovnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Just slower so that these names can be put in the transcript. Start again, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: So towards Medjugorje, there were the village of Miljkovici, towards Siroki Brijeg, Zovnica. There were toward Goranci, up at the curve above Cim, towards Varda on Rudnik and down there from Rodoc -- towards Rodoc towards Dubrovnic, I don't know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if there were any arrests in the town and who engaged in those arrests?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: The police, military or the civilian, doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what kind of vehicles did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: We had from trucks, that is a blue Deutz, and we also had a van.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, now we shall show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: -- D2/23. Can you tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I guess this is the Vinko Martinovic's ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Is there any indication of rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And what does it say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It says, "Soldier."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did Vinko Martinovic have any rank during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It was always a soldier. What do I know? Foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation? After all, he commanded the unit of sorts. How is it that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: He didn't want a title. He was just a plain soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. President, I have no further questions. This is the end of my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Cross-examination, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if I heard you correctly you said that before you were a member of the Mrmak or Vinko Skrobo unit, you were previously a member of the HVO 4th Battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the witness please come closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where were you positioned during the time that were you a member of the 4th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, I was in the 4th Battalion. I guarded the front line. It was the war against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where were you on the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So in the Mostar region; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. It's a hill above Mostar where there were Serbs, I guarded so that they wouldn't break into our houses and so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who was your commander in that unit, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Tihomir Misic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, other than holding a position on the -- what was then considered the front line, did you actually ever engage in combat, that is actual exchange of fire with the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: With Serbs, no. I only guarded the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, sir, that in your position as you've told

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then you told us that you joined Mr. Martinovic's unit a few days, and I think your answers ranged from anywhere from two to five days, after the fighting started in Mostar on about the 9th or 10th of May, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You were in Grude, working, at the time the fighting broke out in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Correct. I left the 4th Battalion to work for the headquarters in Grude as a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So how, during what period of time had you been in Grude before you then returned to Mostar and joined Mr. Martinovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I left in spring, 1992. Well, then, until mid-May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So is it correct, sir, then you continuously away from Mostar and did not return to Mostar, until two to five days after the fighting started in May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I lived in Mostar, against Serbs the shells hit my flat, and my wife was at her father's in Grude so I would come to Mostar to sleep over but I drove all the time. I had no time to come to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, listen to my question, please. Prior to the fighting starting on the 9th of May, 1993, where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: In Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how long had you been in Grude at that time? Had you been there a couple of days? Had you been there a week? Had you been there two months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: A year and two or three months. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you did not return, then, to Mostar, as I indicated a moment ago, and join Mr. Martinovic's unit, until some days after the fighting broke out in Mostar on the 9th and 10th of May, 1993, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, my house is in Mostar, that is my father and my mother and my brother but I couldn't be in Mostar because one room so I spent -- I sleep over and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when I personally conducted the cross-examination during the Prosecution's case, you objected, both you and the Prosecutor, not to repeat questions from the direct. And now, if we talk about the -- I refer to the equality of arms and I objected to the Prosecution doing the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see any harm by asking the question to the witness in this way. You may continue, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The point, sir, is, up until the time that you returned to Mostar, some days after the 9th and 10th of May, 1993, you have absolutely no personal knowledge of what happened on the 8th of May or the 9th of May or the 10th of May, 1993, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I didn't see anything, but I heard from those friends and neighbours, they were preparing for the attack, that they crossed over here and threatened but I wasn't there personally. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is yes, you have no personal knowledge of what happened in Mostar at that time, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Then how long did you stay in Mr. Martinovic's unit? When did you leave the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: When the Washington Agreement was signed. I think it was February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And from approximately mid-May, 1993, sir, to February, 1994, were you a member of any other HVO unit or formation, other than Mr. Martinovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you perform any functions in Mr. Martinovic's unit other than the logistics role that you've described to us this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if I understand your answer a few moments ago, sir, at no time during that time did you engage in combat with the Muslim forces, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, when you weren't moving around in the truck or vehicle that you used, which I'll come back to in a few minutes, where did you spend your time as a member of the Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: When I wasn't working, at home or at my wife's in Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, did you have an office or a desk that you used, for instance, at the Vinko Skrobo headquarters in Kalemova Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I only had a warehouse where I kept those -- this canned food and such like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where was this warehouse located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: On Kalemova Street in that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to repeat my earlier question, sir. Did you have a desk or an office that you used inside the headquarters of Mr. Martinovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Personally, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, please, approximately how many times during the full year 1993, well we know you weren't there until at least mid-May, so from middle of May of 1993, until December of 1993, approximately how many times would you say you were inside the headquarters of the Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: During working hours, for instance from 8.00 to 2 or 3, at times until dusk, at times never. I'd sleep at homes and over weekends I'd go to my wife. At times I went to Germany with my truck, two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you how many times where you -- when you were on duty. I asked you specifically how many times were you in the headquarters, inside the building where Mr. Martinovic had his headquarters, from the middle of May, 1993 until December, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: How many times?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Every day during working days. Mostly I told you except when I was away, and when I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you receive orders from Mr. Martinovic? Or directions from him to do things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Why, no, I didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who gave you your orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I didn't receive any orders. I knew how to procure food. I would go on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So your testimony to the Chamber, to these Judges, sir, is that between May of 1993 and February of 1994, you never received an order from anyone in the Vinko Skrobo or Mrmak unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes. He sends me to do something but not an order to do, nothing specific. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In terms of salaries provided to the unit, you said you went to get the money somewhere but where did you get the money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: From the main staff, from the HVO, like the whole HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where did you physically go to pick up the money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: To Grude.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How often would you do that? Once a week, once a month? How often?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Once a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And would this be -- the money was received in cash, what we might call cash, it was currency?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then you said would you take the money, if I heard your testimony correctly, then you said you took the money, "Down there." What did you mean, "Down there"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Because Grude is higher. That's what we -- how we say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, where did you take the money? Where did you physically then -- you picked up the money in Grude. Where did you take it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I take it to the base and distribute it among the soldiers who were there. Those who were there. Those who weren't had to wait for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you personally hand the currency to the soldiers? I mean from your hand to theirs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Some I did. When I wasn't there, deputies, sometimes Vinko, I leave, and like that, but mostly I.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did the Vinko Skrobo unit have any communications equipment, radios or Motorolas, what some of us might call walkie-talkies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: There were two Motorolas, radios, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where did communication equipment for the unit come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, the town defence got them. One was on the front line, the other one at the base, to notify, in case of an attack or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the vehicles that you used, in connection with the Vinko Skrobo unit, including the vehicles that you drove around, where did those vehicles come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: We only had a blue Deutz, a neighbour from Balinovac gave it to us. We bought the van and we all had our own cars. And later on, we also got, I don't know, sometime around December, a Lada Niva from Grude, a new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say from Grude, you're saying you got from the HVO main logistics base in Grude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. I went there to get it but it was for the town defence. It said it was from Grude. I went to Grude to get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when the unit needed ammunition, whatever the standard infantry round was, perhaps 7.62 millimetre, but when the unit needed ammunition, where did you go for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: We got it from the town defence of Mostar, and some from Grude but those were small quantities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, when you say you got it from the town defence, where did you physically go in Mostar to obtain these items?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: The faculty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, have you got a picture so I can show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, perhaps can you give us a street name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Next to the town stadium, next to the town stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say the faculty, sir, which faculty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, all the faculties are there, the university.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is this where the military police was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, yes, yes, yes, yes, yes, right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This is at the mechanical engineering faculty, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, I read law. I know where law is. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall telling a man named Alojz Salkic that in fact all of Stela's support came from Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: What Salkic? Who is he?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You don't recall telling a man that, in fact, all the support for Mr. Martinovic's unit came from Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No. Alojz Salkic, Alojz is a Croat name and Salkic is a Muslim surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You said sir, that in May, 1993, there were 35 to 40 men in the Vinko Skrobo unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: About that, yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did that remain the same throughout 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, how did it change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Because men came and joined, those who were in other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me direct your attention to approximately August, September, 1993. How many -- excuse me, how many soldiers would you say were in the Vinko Skrobo unit at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: 65, 70, maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At any time, sir, during 1993, was the Vinko Skrobo unit more -- did it have more members than 65 to 70 maximum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I don't think so. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, there is approximately 24 persons in this courtroom. So you're saying that the Vinko Skrobo unit was about from two to three times as many people in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: About that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was there anybody in the Vinko Skrobo unit that you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Perhaps for a day or two or three if I wasn't there and he came. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Generally speaking, sir, this was a small unit and with a possible few exceptions, isn't it correct that you knew every one -- you knew every member of the unit, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know him really. I knew him like this. When I'd see him. But I didn't know who he was or what he was. How could I? But generally, I knew them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, it was a small unit. You got the ammunition for the unit. You handed them their pay. You handed currency to them for pay. You more or less knew every member of the unit, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you drove a truck one time around Zagreb. What were you doing in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: It's when I worked in Grude. I drove from Zagreb all the time, food and clothing, humanitarian aid. But when I was with Vinko Martinovic, I went to Germany three times in my own truck. Normally I asked Vinko to let me go, and he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's stay on Zagreb for a moment or two. How many times when you were working at the main base, this is the main logistics base of the HVO in Grude, how many times were you going back and forth to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Every week.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What were you driving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I went in my own truck, the army gave me their numbers and of course recruited me and they paid fuel so that I would go so relief comes from the Netherlands for this church for this parish, people who collected food and all that and it would reach Zagreb by train and I would reload it and then take it down to, I don't know, places in west Herzegovina, Mostar, church, I did it every day, food, clothing. And I was a member of this logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are you suggesting to the Chamber, sir, that you never transported arms or ammunition or military materiel from Zagreb to Grude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes. During the war with the Serbs, but then we unloaded that in Capljina and then this load went onwards to Capljina. But this did not belong to us. It belonged to some other organisation. I don't know which organisation that was. And then it went on to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, part of the answer was missed. The witness said that from Capljina, the load went to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said that. And that was during the war against Serbs but the question was about the ammunition, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, where did the shipments with the ammunition go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: We unloaded it did in Capljina, then somebody came, I don't know who, that was in 1992, during the war with the Serbs, at the beginning of the war, I don't know who they were, who, why. Muslims. To them, it was not to me. It was to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, during the fighting with the Muslims, sir in 1993, the war between the Croats and the Muslims, how many times did you go to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Not once. I was -- later on, when I left Markovic, then I took my truck and then I drove normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You drove normally. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: I was a hauler. I transported goods all over Europe. I transported goods for companies, for private individuals. I was not an army member. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In 1993, sir, you were not an army member? From May, 1993, until the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honours, I have to intervene. I don't know, are we sitting in two different courtrooms? My learned friend and me? Or maybe the interpretation is so terrible or maybe the witness is just doing a bad job speaking. Now the Prosecution asked something that the witness has already repeated a hundred -- 480 times where he was in May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, this witness is not your witness. You have to keep silent, I'm afraid. It doesn't -- the testimony of this witness has nothing to do with your client at this moment. I don't see any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am trying to assist you with the testimony of this witness. I'm trying to help you understand this witness, and I believe that it is all for the benefit of justice. If something is missing -- misinterpreted or lost in the transcript then I believe it is my place to assist this Chamber to understand this witness correctly. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I only see a problem there. The witness answered, "I'm a hauler. I transported goods all over Europe. I transported goods for companies, for private individuals. I was not an army member." Then the witness wanted to say something and Mr. Scott cut in. "In 1993, sir, you were not an army member from May 1993, until the end of 1993." Are there any misunderstandings?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, you have framed the issue and that's exactly why I asked the question because I asked what he was doing and where he was driving about in 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the next thing he was telling us was that in 1993 he wasn't in the army, that he was hauling for private companies, that he was acting as a private person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, so maybe there is a misunderstanding. Mr. Scott, would you please re-ask your question so we could get a definite answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course exactly the question I was going to put before Mr. Krsnik --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never said this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, forget what was said in the last few minutes. Let me put a new question to you. You've told us this afternoon that you were driving a truck a vehicle, at various times, you've mentioned going to Grude, frequently, going to Zagreb, going to Germany. How much of your time during 1993 were you actually in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: From mid-May until December, on three occasions, I went to Germany on private business, and I spent several weekends with my wife in Grude. I've already repeated this five times. After the end of 1993, in February, 1994, I stopped being an army member and then I continued doing my job proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, when you delivered the currency, the salary, to the soldiers of the Vinko Skrobo unit, you delivered that at the headquarters on Kalemova Street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you delivered ammunition, where did you deliver the ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MT
utterances.text: Let me tell you. Every day there was a certain number of bullets for a certain number of soldiers. Two or three grenades. And some bullets.
